narrative:
Current integration, based on the thermal-protected OS at 6d77a16d; evidence in ~/.cache/sunstoneos/evidence/resume-perf-modes-1025/ (final snapshot manifest final-snapshot/manifest.json: 28 engine cases, 21 CPU-owner and 22 combined-owner cases, eight host-command cases, 44 producer/launcher cases and seven native combined admission/USB cases; the native check reuses the existing OS NPU instruction model, RTOS and device effects modeled). The owner takes 30 modeled ticks for its boot switch. A thousand idle ticks add no register reads, PMIC snapshots or device requests. Cleanup contention retries the same snapshot within its original deadline and adds no snapshot submission. CPU and combined NPU profiles link natively. The owner checks include thermal interruption before and during a switch, NORMAL returning before an active change finishes, snapshot interruption, transient cleanup contention and retained timeout failures. The combined native fixture exercises the actual 1176-byte session admission and both USB diagnostics (thermal operation 7 and performance operation 8). The source-backed engine retains three CPU requests and two PMIC selector writes per full switch. The shared PLL lock helper takes 233 modeled microseconds and 43 lock samples per stopped-NPU retune, with five writes and 19 or 20 register reads. Both profiles link with the current thermal diagnostic and its session CPU trip. Sizes (.text, .rodata, .bss) include the thermal evidence window: CPU performance with high boot 903,584, 43,689, 1,567,264; CPU and NPU performance with low boot 983,840, 47,801, 1,707,808.

Earlier implementation (17b63bd2), host models and builds, evidence ~/.cache/sunstoneos/evidence/perf-modes-20261025/; the models give each CPU domain change a fixed modeled cost (1 ms voltage settle and 0.1 ms relock per CPU change; owner stepped once per 1 ms tick), so wall times show the service's own overhead and ordering. checks/perf-mode.py engine model (checks/perf-mode-model.c): 3 CPU driver requests per full switch (CPU-L, CPU-B, DSU); 2 PMIC selector writes (DCDC5, DCDC3); boot switch from boot0's state 5.0 ms; high to low and low to high 5.4 ms each; NPU held after its session stops 0.4 ms (the modeled retune); refusal of a switch whose NPU session stays open 1.5 s (the hold bound). checks/npu-startup-host.c --retune: 5 PLL_NPU writes each read back; 19 or 20 register reads, 70 lock samples, 2 register-lock acquisitions; modeled retune 228 us. checks/perf-os-model.c: boot switch with readback 30 owner ticks; 4 PMIC snapshots per readback (DCDC5, DCDC3, DCDC4, DCDC2).
Image sizes of that implementation (llvm-size-21 -A; .text, .rodata, .bss): CPU clock build (A733_A76_ADMITTED, SUNSTONE_A733_OS_CPU_CLOCK) 890,400, 43,129, 1,532,576; the same with SUNSTONE_A733_OS_PERF 899,808 (+9,408), 43,321 (+192), 1,533,408 (+832); NPU profile 952,352, 45,721, 1,672,352; NPU profile with the CPU clock owner and the service, low boot mode 979,936 (+27,584), 47,513 (+1,792), 1,674,016 (+1,664); the second NPU row's growth includes the CPU clock driver and its owner, which the NPU profile did not link before.
Default images: the ten default OS variants were built from clean archives at one path at the branch base (fc889bba, the CPU top-point merge) and at 17b63bd2 with the same mimus checkout (9c57286b), and their loadable segments compared (images/comparison.json in the evidence directory). The OS build identity hashes every apps/os header and the changed board sources, so the 32-byte a733_smp_build_id differs in every image. Variants sup, res, resaud, resradio, resradioaud, headset, resheadset, radio-headset, resradio-headset: loadable bytes equal apart from the build identity. Variant npu: equal segment layout and symbol sizes; besides the build identity, 165 bytes differ, all inside a733_npu_startup_step. The NPU difference is code generation, not behaviour: lock_wait now has a second caller, the stopped-NPU retune, which the linker then discards from this image. Forced inline at both callers the step keeps its 5,596 bytes with a few loads and adds placed differently (287 ldr instead of 282 plus 5 ldur); without the forced inline the first revision (ec0fe8da) called lock_wait as a 316-byte function. The startup host model (checks/npu-startup-host.c, every mode) passes on the source. Gate perf-modes-20261025-2 built all twelve OS variants (the ten defaults and both performance-mode variants) at 17b63bd2 and verified the check index.

hypothesis: Vendor sequence for a run-time GPU operating-point change, derived during review
narrative: Derived reference the GPU owner follows (docs/designs/gpu-performance.md holds the implemented path). The vendor build defines SUPPORT_LINUX_DVFS (binary_sunxi_linux_nulldrmws_release/config_kernel.h:37), so the change runs through the DDK's devfreq target (pvr_dvfs_device.c, not pinned). RGXProcessCoreClkChangeRequest (rgxpower.c:1708-1768, SHA-256 77cf1473) shows the same order under SUPPORT_PDVFS: an idle request (bIdleReq, sysconfig.c:366; PVRSRVDevicePreClockSpeedChange, power.c:1313-1367); the voltage before the frequency when raising and after it when lowering (rgxpower.c:1751-1763); then the timer correlation, the firmware's core-clock word and the CORECLKSPEEDCHANGE command (:1160-1215); and the idle cancel. A denied idle request is a refusal. With the GPU off there is no idle request and no command. sunxiSetFrequency (sunxi_platform.c:405-471, SHA-256 35fa7f99) runs rates above 800 MHz from PLL_GPU0 and 600 MHz from PERI0's 600 MHz output, through the GPU clock word at CCU +0xb20 (mux bits 24-26, divider table in bits 0-3, update key bit 27; ccu-sun60iw2.c:1020-1043). PLL_GPU0 stays enabled and locked while the core runs from PERI0. DCDC4 settles |dV| / 250 uV per us rounded up to 1 ms (axp2101-regulator.c:383-408), and sunxiSetVoltage then waits 200 us (sunxi_platform.c:473-485). The GPU's low point reads opp-microvolt-vfdefault because its device tree has no speed-bin map for the GPU: in that column 400 and 600 MHz run at 800 mV and 800 MHz needs 840 mV (the vf0400 column itself lists 900 mV for 1008 MHz while the vendor kernel applies 960 mV and the board ran it).
